title: With the documented default `n = NULL`, every completeness check and every Inference constructor fails with "argument is of length zero", so an open-enrollment trial can never be analyzed
KK14 / KK21 accept `n = NULL` at construction but the 5th assignment fails with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" and leaves the design corrupted (t advances, no w stored)
KK14/KK21 constructors accept `lambda` outside [0, 1] (and `t_0_pct` outside [0, 1]); the failure surfaces later, mid-trial, as base-R messages that do not name the argument
`InferenceContinKKGLMM` parametric bootstrap has almost no spread: the 95% CI is ~70x narrower than the Wald CI and the p-value sits at its minimum

`InferenceSuite$run_all_inference()` with `max_secs_per_class` and `num_cores = 2` prints the whole report and then fails with "arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0", so no results object is returned
With `n = NULL`, outcomes can only be recorded in enrollment order; an out-of-order outcome for an enrolled subject is refused with the false message "subject that has not yet arrived"
After `compute_rand_two_sided_pval()`, `InferenceAllSimpleMeanDiffPooledVar`'s asymptotic p-value and CI silently become `NA`

`DesignFixedRerandomization` with `prop_acceptable` assigns the real allocation from a different distribution than the one its randomization test uses as reference, and the randomization test over-rejects
`DesignFixedGreedy` and `DesignFixedGreedyDOptimal` with defaults and the same seed do not return the same allocations when covariates have ties
`DesignFixedOptimal(objective = "abs_sum_diff")` with the default `solver = "auto"` does not finish for n = 40, with no message
`get_optimization_diagnostics()$objective_value` is not the documented objective M(w): it is M/4 for "mahal_dist" and M/2 for "abs_sum_diff"
Every fixed design's constructor takes the default `n = NULL`, then the first `add_all_subjects_to_experiment()` errors, although `X_all` supplies n

DesignFixedBlockedCluster with unequal block sizes errors with a message telling the user to set `equal_block_sizes = FALSE` or pass `B_target`, but the class accepts neither argument (not in the constructor, not in `assign_w_to_all_subjects()`)

`approximate_bootstrap_distribution_beta_hat_T(bootstrap_type = ...)` returns the cached draws from an earlier call with a different `bootstrap_type` on the same inference object, so `"resample_blocks"` silently gives the `"within_blocks"` distribution (or vice versa)

On `DesignFixedBlockedCluster`, the cluster warnings lead in a circle: `edi_cluster_independence_warning` recommends the jackknife with `unit = "cluster"`, which returns NA and says to use `unit = "block"`, which returns NA and says to use "the model-based standard error", the very SE the first warning said is too narrow

`assign_w_to_all_subjects(w_precomputed = )` accepts a 1/2-coded treatment on `DesignFixedCluster`, keeps it as 1/2, and `InferenceAllSimpleAverageDiff` then returns `NA` estimate and `NA` randomization p-value with no warning
`n = NULL`, the default shown in `?DesignFixedCluster` and `?DesignFixedBlockedCluster`, fails at the first step, and the follow-up error is unhelpful
`DesignFixedCluster$assign_w_to_all_subjects(w_precomputed = )` accepts a pupil-level assignment that varies within schools, with no warning, and cluster inference runs on it

On a blocked-cluster trial, `compute_bootstrap_confidence_interval(type = "prepivoted" | "double-bootstrap" | "calibrated")` returns `c(NA, NA)` with only the reason "bootstrap_ci_unavailable", even though `get_supported_bootstrap_ci_types()` lists these types and the percentile interval on the same object is finite

`?DesignFixedBlockedCluster` does not say that every block must hold the same number of subjects, or that the jackknife (every `unit`) returns NA on this design; both are stated only in the web article

Randomization tests refuse every incidence analysis on `DesignFixedFactorial` and `DesignFixedBlocking`, yet `supports("randomization_test")` is TRUE and the factorial article says these designs work like any two-arm design
The error tells the user to "Use Zhang method", but `type = "Zhang"` then fails with a message claiming the outcome is not incidence

On the 2 x 2 main-effect design (`DesignFixedBlocking` with 2 blocks) the default bootstrap CI and p-value (BCa) and every jackknife unit return NA, and the warning recommends a randomization test that errors for this outcome
`DesignFixedFactorial` accepts a non-integer number of levels (`list(subject = 2.5)`) and silently runs it as a two-level factor
The same marginal risk ratio is reported on the log scale by `InferenceIncidLogRegr` (`estimand = "marginal_ratio"`) but on the ratio scale by `InferenceIncidGCompRiskRatio`

The unequal-block error says "strata_cols was named without B_target" even when `B_target` was passed, and suggests passing `B_target`, which does not help; the help also says the check fires when subjects are added, but it fires at assignment

`InferenceIncidExactFisher$compute_estimate()` returns a bare `NA` with no warning when one arm has no events, while its exact CI and p-value are finite and `fisher.test`/`mantelhaen.test` give an odds ratio of `Inf`
`InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr` with its default L-BFGS optimizer stops short of the Weibull MLE, so the time-ratio estimate and Wald CI disagree with `survival::survreg` in the 3rd significant digit
`fast_weibull_regression(use_rcpp = FALSE)` reports "failed to converge" when the real problem is an empty column name in `X`
An exact event time of 0 is accepted by the design, and `InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr` then returns `NA` estimate, CI and p-value with no warning

`InferenceSurvivalKMDiff$compute_asymp_two_sided_pval()` returns `NA` while `compute_asymp_confidence_interval()` on the same object is finite, and the warning's fix (`na.rm = TRUE`) cannot be passed to the method the user called

On interval-censored data, `InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr` lists score / gradient / lik_ratio as supported testing types and accepts `set_testing_type("score")`, but then gives NA, a Wald interval relabelled, or an error, depending on which method is called
Error messages for survival classes point users to repo-internal design documents that are not shipped with the package
`?InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff` names a design class, `DesignFixedBCRD`, that does not exist
`InferenceSuite$run_all_inference()` prints `p = NA` for every estimand that has only one inference class, although that class's p-value is finite in the same table

On interval-censored data, `InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr`'s Wald CI and p-value change with the global RNG state even after `set_seed()`, so the "asymptotic" p-value is not reproducible from the object's seed
A `model_formula` naming a covariate that was entirely `NA` (silently removed under `"impute"`) gives an `NA` estimate and `c(NA, NA)` CI, with only an unrelated `cbind` recycling warning
With `missingness_method = "error"`, covariate-adaptive sequential designs assign the first subjects despite their `NA` covariates, then fail on a later subject whose own data are complete
A failed `add_one_subject_to_experiment_and_assign()` (the `"error"` refusal) still enrolls the subject: `get_t()` goes up and `w` is left `NA`
An `Inf` covariate is accepted at enrollment; inference then fails with an internal `qr.default` error
When `"drop_column"` removes every covariate, covariate-balancing designs (rerandomization, KK14, greedy, Atkinson) silently run without any covariates
The docs say "EDI 1.0.4 and earlier" gave the outcome to the imputation model, but the installed package is version 1.0.4 and does not
In sequential designs, `get_X_raw()` and `get_X()` reorder the covariate columns when the first subject has missing values
`get_summary()` on `InferenceContinOLS` prints only the treatment row, though the docs promise the full coefficient table for model-based classes

`transform_responses = "log"` on a continuous response applies an incoherent sharp null: treated responses are divided by e^delta to impute controls, but delta is then added (not multiplied) back to the units treated in each draw.
`transform_responses` accepts any string (e.g. `"bogus"`, `"sqrt"`, `"identity"`) silently, and the set of allowed values is not documented.
`r` between 1 and 9 is accepted (the check is only `r >= 1`) but the p-value is then always `NA` with no warning, because at least 10 finite draws are required.

The CI refusal for count and proportion responses tells the user the "randomization-bootstrap CI remain[s] available", but InferenceRandCustom has no bootstrap CI (its own help and `capabilities()` say only the randomization test and CI exist); the message also points to internal repo files.

For survival responses InferenceRandCustom advertises and returns a randomization CI (and accepts nonzero `delta`), although the article says these are for continuous responses only and the help says survival CIs invert a log-time shift that a raw-scale statistic cannot match; count/proportion with the same scale mismatch are refused.
Nonzero `delta` is silently accepted for count and proportion responses, which the article calls "not a coherent hypothesis"; incidence refuses it with an error.
C++ source that defines any helper function (even a forward-declared or `inline` one), or uses the usual `// [[Rcpp::export]]` tag, is rejected; the help says only "C++ source defining a function".
Passing the C++ source as a character vector of several lines gives an error that says the value is "not a character", although it is one.
The article says a two-argument statistic `function(y, w)` "fails with 'unused argument (dead)'", but EDI rejects it with a different message.

An `InferenceCustomRand` subclass whose `fit()` calls a user-defined helper function returns a randomization p-value (and CI) of `NA` with no warning when 2 cores are set; with 1 core it gives the correct value.

The `permutations` argument ("Optional pre-generated assignment draws" / "Pre-computed permutations") has no documented format; an n x r matrix fails with an unrelated error, and malformed draws (wrong length, 1/2 coding) are accepted silently.
The article states the two-sided p-value has "a floor of 2/r", but when draws are dropped the floor is 2/B (B = number of finite draws), as the InferenceRand help says.
`import edi_kernels` kills the Python interpreter with SIGILL ("Illegal instruction", exit code 132) on an AVX2-only x86-64 CPU, so no kernel can be called
The README and the article contradict each other on whether the kernels check that `w` is 0/1
The `fast_coxph_regression` docstring does not say how tied event times are handled (Breslow or Efron), so a 3-digit cross-check against lifelines/statsmodels cannot be set up from the docs

With `compute_conf_intervals = FALSE`, `run_all_inference()` still emits rows for CI-only bootstrap types (`basic`, `calibrated`, `prepivoted`, ...) with `pval = NA`, no message, `status = "ok"`, and `pval_method`/`ci_method` filled in, contrary to the help page

The suite's `estimand` column labels Poisson, negative-binomial and hurdle-Poisson fits as `log_rate_ratio_marginal`, while the objects themselves report `get_estimand() == "conditional"`; hurdle NB (same kind of coefficient as hurdle Poisson) is labelled `log_rate_ratio_conditional`, so Combined Evidence groups and weights are built on inconsistent labels

`max_secs_per_class` does not give a `"timeout"` row: when the limit fires it escapes `run_all_inference()` (and an enclosing `tryCatch`) and aborts the R session, and classes that run far past the limit are still reported `ok`

A misspelled `type` in a list-shaped `methods` (e.g. `bootstrap = "percentil"`) is silently accepted: the row comes back with `type = NA`, a numeric p-value from an unnamed bootstrap flavour, `status = "ok"` and no message

`print()`, `summary()` and `combined_evidence` count result rows as "classes": the header says "300 class(es)" for 11 classes, `summary()` says "classes: 2" then "ok: 6", and `n_classes_used` includes rows that got weight 0
The printed per-estimand Combined Evidence line shows `p = NA` for an estimand group with a single inference, although that p-value is valid and is used in the overall combined p-value

When a class's randomization CI errors ("not supported"), `run_all_inference(compute_conf_intervals = TRUE)` reports `ci_a = ci_b = NA` with `ci_method = "rand"`, `status = "ok"`, an empty `message` and no warning, so the explanation is lost

The "Randomization confidence intervals are not supported" error for InferenceCountQuasiPoisson says the class's estimate "is on the raw response scale", which is false (it is a log rate ratio, identical to InferenceCountPoisson's, whose randomization CI works), and it points to an internal TODO file path

The printed suite table wraps a negative number in scientific notation across two lines and mangles it: `-4.22e-06` is shown as `-4.22e--` with `06` on the next line (`-8.47e-05` as `-8.47e--` / `05` on my trial)

`?InferenceSuite` tells users to consult `EDI_INFERENCE_SUITE_METHOD_SENTINELS` and `is_inference_class_compatible_with_design_metadata()`, but neither is exported or documented, so neither can be inspected

After `set_num_cores(2)`, `run_all_inference(num_cores = 2L)` breaks the persistent cluster: one class's randomization p-value fails with "ignoring SIGPIPE signal" while its row stays `status = "ok"`, and later direct `compute_rand_two_sided_pval()` calls in the same session fail too
`InferenceCountRobustPoisson` returns its estimate and p-values as a value named `"treatment"`, while every other class (Poisson, QuasiPoisson, NegBin, ...) returns unnamed numbers
`InferenceCountNegBin`'s score p-value depends on whether the score CI was computed first on the object, so the same suite row differs between `compute_conf_intervals = FALSE` and `TRUE`

Bootstrap on a KK14/KK21 sequential design stops with "This method is not supported for DesignSeqOneByOne designs", but the same call works on another DesignSeqOneByOne design, and the KK analysis help page lists the bootstrap as one of its methods

`clone(deep = TRUE)` of a stratified sequential design (SPBR, RandomBlockSize, PocockSimon) shares the per-stratum state with the original: advancing the copy changes the original's later assignments and breaks SPBR's permuted blocks

After a restore, one covariate value arriving as text silently converts that covariate to character for every earlier subject, dummy-codes it, changes later assignments, and the final analysis returns `NA` estimate, `NA` CI and `NA` p-value with no warning

The installed package reports version 1.0.4 and stamps saved designs "1.0.4", but the docs describe its sequential seeding as "v1.0.6" behaviour and say that earlier versions seeded differently, so a trial file's version stamp points to the wrong allocation rule
A sequential design with a fixed `n` silently accepts subject n + 1; `check_experiment_completed()` then returns `TRUE` and inference analyzes n + 1 subjects while `get_n()` still reports n
The notation-glossary vignette says `SimulationFramework` custom hooks receive `w` in {-1,+1}, but they receive {0,1} (as `?SimulationFramework` says)
`?SimulationFramework` tells users to call `$get_errors()` after `$run()`, but `SimulationFramework` objects have no `get_errors` method
`?SimulationFramework` says `$run()` returns a `SimulationFrameworkReport`, and also that it returns the `SimulationFramework` object; the second is true
With `num_cores = 1`, `SimulationFramework` does not seed replication i with `seed + i`, so the same `seed` gives different results at `num_cores = 1` and `num_cores = 2`
Resuming a serial (`num_cores = 1`) run with `continue_from_last_result_row = TRUE` replays the first replications' data as the new replications, so the "extra" replications are duplicates

`alpha` is checked with a message about `'p'` (which is also the name of the covariate-count argument), and `alpha = 0` is accepted, giving infinite CIs that `summarize()` then reports as coverage `NA`
A negative `sd_noise` is not rejected; the run then fails with a message about missing outcomes and a link to the missing-data article

A design parameter the constructor does not accept makes the whole cell vanish with a warning about design/inference compatibility, even with `stop_on_error = TRUE`; the real cause (unused argument) is never shown
`SimulationFrameworkReport$new(sim, alpha = a)` keeps the CIs built at the framework's alpha but tests their coverage against `1 - a`, so `coverage_pval` flags correctly calibrated intervals

For `response_type = "incidence"`, `SimulationFramework` scores `InferenceIncidGCompRiskDiff` against the logit-scale `betaT` instead of a risk difference, so its reported coverage is 0 and its MSE is wrong
`n = NULL`, the documented default of every fixed design constructor (incl. `ObservationalDesign`), fails as soon as the data are added
On an `ObservationalDesign`, the inference object's `capabilities()` / `supports()` still report randomization tests, randomization CIs and randomization bootstrap, which then refuse to run
`InferenceSuite$run_all_inference(num_cores = 2)` after `set_num_cores(2)` silently loses some p-values (`NA`, status `"ok"`) and gives the message "ignoring SIGPIPE signal"
Help pages for the observational / existing-data path point users to internal developer files that are not shipped with the package
With `w_precomputed` all 0 (nobody treated), `InferenceContinOLS` reports a covariate's slope as the "treatment effect", with a CI and p-value and no warning
`assign_w_to_all_subjects(w_precomputed = )` accepts treatment codes other than 0/1 (1/2, a factor, 0.5) without a word, while `overwrite_all_subject_assignments()` rejects them
A `w_precomputed` of the wrong length is silently recycled to length n; the only signal is base R's recycling warning
An `NA` in `w_precomputed` is accepted and stored; it fails only later, inside the model fit, with "Error in qr.default(X_mat) : NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 1)"
`DesignFixedBinaryMatch` with an explicit pairing `m` accepts a `w_precomputed` that treats both members of one pair and neither of another, then runs a within-pair randomization test on it

With unequal strata and the default `equal_block_sizes = TRUE`, the error comes neither "when subjects are added" (help page) nor at "an inference fit" (article); it comes only at the first bootstrap or randomization call

The article says the default BCa bootstrap interval for the four-site trial is `NA` with a warning (leave-one-site-out jackknife needs at least 5 sites); it actually returns a finite interval with no warning
`InferenceIncidCMH` is listed as applicable to an `ObservationalDesign`, but its asymptotic (Wald) p-value tries to redraw `w` and fails with an internal design error

Risk-ratio classes report the treatment effect on different scales: `InferenceIncidGCompRiskRatio` returns the raw ratio (null 1, `delta = 0` errors), while `InferenceIncidLogBinomial`, `InferenceIncidModifiedPoisson` and `InferenceIncidLogRegr` with `estimand = "marginal_ratio"` return the log ratio (null 0)
`InferenceIncidLogBinomial` returns `NA` estimate, `c(NA, NA)` CI and `NA` p-value without any warning when one arm has zero events; `glm(binomial(link = "log"))` gives a finite boundary fit
`InferenceIncidModifiedPoisson` on zero-cell data reports log RR = -22.3, 95% CI (-22.85, -21.80) and p-value exactly 0, with no boundary or separation warning

`InferenceIncidExactFisher$compute_estimate()` returns `NA` without a warning when a cell is zero, although `fisher.test` gives a conditional MLE of 0 (log OR = -Inf) and the class's own exact CI has lower bound `-Inf`

The public `compute_lik_ratio_bartlett_exact_*()` methods of `InferenceIncidLogRegr` return `NA` with the warning text "Reason: no error message was recorded", and the `set_testing_type()` error lists `lik_ratio_bartlett_exact` as allowed although the class then refuses it

On matched-pair data with zero events in the treated arm, the KK conditional-logit classes return `NA` estimate/CI/p-value (OneLik, GLMM) or a meaningless CI of about ±21 500 (IVWC) with no warning at all

On a complete-randomization (`DesignFixediBCRD`) incidence design, `compute_rand_two_sided_pval()` says "Use Zhang method", but passing `type = "Zhang"` fails with "Randomization type dispatch is only supported for incidence outcomes" although the outcome is incidence

`InferenceIncidLogRegr`'s parametric-bootstrap estimate and CI silently include near-separated replicates (log OR about -25). The "bias-corrected" estimate flips the sign of a strong protective effect (-2.23 becomes +1.03) and the CI upper bound is +21, while the diagnostics report `n_extreme = 0`

On zero-cell data `InferenceSuite$run_all_inference()` marks `InferenceIncidExactFisher` "nonest" and drops its valid exact p-value and CI from the table and from the combined evidence, but keeps separated fits flagged by their own warnings (GComp RR p = 0, CI 2.7e-10 to 7.6e-10) as "ok" with full weight
`?InferenceIncidWald` and `?InferenceIncidRiskDiff` document constructor arguments (`alpha`, `delta`; `r`, `delta`, `type`, `permutations`, ...) that `$new()` does not accept
`model_formula_zero = ~ 1` (ZIP/ZINB) and `model_formula_hurdle = ~ 1` (hurdle) quietly fit a zero/hurdle part of `~ w`, not the intercept-only part the user asked for

For ZIP and hurdle Poisson, `get_summary()` prints a model-based SE and p-value for the treatment, but `compute_asymp_*` use a sandwich SE. The two disagree (p = 0.093 vs 0.299) and the summary does not say which SE it shows

`InferenceCountHurdleNegBin$get_summary()` gives `NA` for every Std. Error, z and p-value, although the class computes a finite Wald SE. It also drops the hurdle part and uses different row labels from the other two-part classes
An `offset(log_fu)` term in `model_formula` is accepted and echoed back by `get_model_formula()`, but it is silently dropped. The fit equals the no-offset fit in Poisson, NegBin and ZIP

`InferenceCountKKGLMM`'s Wald CI and p-value use the jackknife SE, not the "model-based GLMM standard error" the help page promises. `get_summary()` labels that SE as the model's Std. Error with `use_rcpp = TRUE`, but shows the real model SE with `use_rcpp = FALSE`

`InferenceCountKKGLMM$get_supported_testing_types()` lists `"lik_ratio_bartlett_approx"`, and `set_testing_type()` accepts it, but `compute_asymp_confidence_interval()` / `compute_asymp_two_sided_pval()` then fail with "Unsupported testing_type"

When every control subject has a zero count, Poisson, QuasiPoisson and RobustPoisson return a randomization p-value of exactly 1 for every `alternative`, with no warning. Once the separated fit exists, every randomization refit returns the observed estimate (22.79) unchanged

`InferenceOrdinalPartialProportionalOddsRegr` with no non-parallel covariates gives a different CI and p-value than `InferenceOrdinalPropOddsRegr` on the same fit, because it quietly uses a t(n-1) reference instead of the normal.
`nonparallel` accepts a covariate name that does not exist and silently fits the full proportional-odds model.

`benchmark_asymp_two_sided_pval_breakdown()` returns a different estimate, SE and p-value from `compute_estimate()` / `compute_asymp_two_sided_pval()`, although the docs say it runs the same computation.
The proportional-odds, cloglog, probit and cauchit classes do not document their own constructor, and the inherited `Inference$new()` documents `harden` and `seed`, which these constructors reject.

The R6 cumulative-link classes report point estimates that are not at the MLE: they differ from `ordinal::clm` and from EDI's own C++ backend in the 3rd significant digit (up to 0.0036 for cauchit), so the Wald CI and p-value are off too.

`compute_asymp_confidence_interval()` on `InferenceOrdinalPropOddsRegr` (Wald) and `InferenceOrdinalRidit` accepts alpha outside (0, 1): alpha = 1.5 silently returns a reversed interval, and alpha < 0 returns NaN.
The alpha check says "Element 1 is not <= 1" when alpha = 1, which is <= 1.

When every patient is in the same category, `InferenceOrdinalRidit` returns estimate 0 with NA CI and NA p-value, with no warning and `is_nonestimable() == FALSE`. `InferenceOrdinalPropOddsRegr` returns a finite estimate of 0 for an unidentified model.

Under quasi-complete separation (every treated patient in the lowest category), `InferenceOrdinalPropOddsRegr` reports a huge Wald estimate and CI with no warning and no non-estimable flag, and its likelihood-ratio CI is `NA NA` with no warning.

`InferenceSuite`'s combined-evidence Cauchy combination quietly floors every input p-value at 1e-4, so the "combined" p (1.05e-4) is larger than 19 of the 21 p-values it combines and 27x the Liu–Xie value.

?InferenceOrdinalJonckheereTerpstraTest says exact enumeration is capped at one million allocations, with a warning and the asymptotic p-value above that. In fact an exact p-value is returned for 2.5e25 allocations, with no warning.

`InferencePropBetaRegr` silently rewrites every response with the Smithson-Verkuilen squeeze when the data has exact 0s or 1s, and the help page points to a `sanitize_beta_response()` that has no documentation
`InferencePropQuantileRegr` silently clamps exact 0s/1s to machine epsilon before the logit, so at a low or high `tau` the "log-odds shift" is about ±34 with p ~ 1e-117 and no warning
`InferencePropQuantileRegr$new(tau = 1)` is rejected with "Element 1 is not <= 1", which is false for 1

`InferencePropZeroOneInflatedBetaRegr` returns an NA CI and p-value with no warning when the data has exact 1s but no exact 0s and a covariate is on its natural scale (age in years); centring the covariate gives a finite answer for the same model
`InferencePropGCompMeanDiff` with `variance_fallback_methods = character(0)` returns an NA point estimate, not just an NA variance, and gives no warning

`InferencePropZeroOneInflatedBetaRegr` accepts a `model_formula_zero_one` that names an unknown variable and returns `NA` with no error or warning; the same typo in `model_formula` gives a clear error

The `"model_based"` variance fallback of `InferencePropGCompMeanDiff` uses the unscaled Bernoulli information, which the fractional-logit help page calls wrong for a fractional response; on this data it is 2.5 times the sandwich SE
`get_supported_estimands()` throws an error on `InferencePropFractionalLogit` instead of returning `"conditional"`, while the other `get_supported_*()` getters return vectors
The jackknife methods of `InferencePropQuantileRegr` return NA even on clean interior data, and the warning blames separation, which a quantile regression on logit(y) cannot have
The proportion cookbook says fractional logit requires open-interval data, but the class help page says Y in [0, 1], and the class fits exact 0s and 1s correctly
